memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For seven days make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will be most holy, and whatever touches it will be holy." - Exodus 29:37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After seven days of atonement, the altar itself becomes most holy — and then something remarkable is said: "whatever touches it will be holy." Holiness moves outward from the altar to whatever comes into contact with it. Contact transfers consecration.

That is worth noticing, because we usually think of contamination spreading rather than holiness. In the ordinary world, the clean thing gets dirty when it touches the dirty thing. But here, at God's altar, the direction reverses. What touches the holy becomes holy.

This is the gospel's direction exactly. When Jesus touched lepers, He did not become unclean — they became clean (Mark 1:41-42). Holiness flowed from Him outward. And that is what happens to us in Christ. We come to the altar defiled and are made holy by contact with the One who is holy. Hebrews says we have been made holy through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all (Heb 10:10). You do not make yourself holy before approaching. You approach, and He makes you holy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I expect my sin to contaminate, or Christ's holiness to cleanse?
Am I approaching Christ as I am, trusting Him to make me holy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, holiness flows from You outward. I come to You as I am, unclean and needing cleansing, and I trust You to make me holy by Your finished work. Amen.
